title: RoMa: A Credibility-Aware Fault-Tolerance Framework for LLM Multi-Agent Systems

abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in collaborative problem-solving across diverse domains. However, their reliability remains a critical challenge due to inherent agent failures, including hallucinations, inconsistent outputs, and communication breakdowns. This paper presents RoMa (Robust Multi-Agent), a novel framework that integrates Bayesian credibility evaluation with adaptive fault tolerance mechanisms to enhance system robustness. RoMa employs three complementary strategies: redundant execution with credibility-weighted voting, primary-backup failover, and dynamic agent isolation with rehabilitation. We formalize the framework as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP) and propose an adversarial training paradigm that systematically injects faults during training to improve resilience. Extensive experiments on collaborative software debugging tasks demonstrate that RoMa achieves significantly higher success rates and substantially better fault detection accuracy compared to baseline approaches under realistic fault conditions, while maintaining comparable computational efficiency. Our results validate the effectiveness of credibility-driven fault tolerance in building more reliable multi-agent LLM systems.
